newsitem.title: CHINA: China destroys 600,000 pirated CDs, videos.
newsitem.headline: China destroys 600,000 pirated CDs, videos.

text.p: Authorities in China's southern province of Guangdong have smashed 600,000 pirated audio and video products as part of a renewed crackdown on such products, the China Youth Daily said on Saturday.
"Under the rumbling wheels of a steamroller, the small mountain of 600,000 illegal audio and video products was crushed to pieces," the newspaper said.
The destruction took place in the provincial capital of Guangzhou amid recent efforts to crack down on violations of intellectual property rights, the newspaper said but gave no further details.
Provincial authorities shut down two factories producing pirated compact discs in September and October, rewarding informants with bounties of 300,000 yuan ($36,000) each, official media has said.
Guangdong has offered the reward to anyone who informs on a pirate compact disc factory, and has set other cash incentives for information on vendors or stockpiles of pirated goods.

China and the United States went to the brink of a multi-billion trade war in June over Washington's accusations that Beijing was not doing enough to combat rampant piracy of intellectual property rights.
Many of China's intellectual property pirates have set up operations in booming Guangdong.
